title: How to read Shakespeare's language
examples: Why is Shakespeare hard to read?

explain.say: Shakespeare wrote over 400 years ago, and his words can look like a secret code. But here is good news: it is English, just older! Look at the board. On the left, thou art. On the right, you are. Thou means you.
Here is a famous line: O Romeo, Romeo, wherefore art thou Romeo? Many people think Juliet is asking where he is. Look at the board: where plus fore. Wherefore actually means why!
So Juliet is asking: Why are you Romeo? She means, why do you have to be from the family my family hates? Look back at the compare board. Can you spot two more old words, hath and anon?
Hath means has, and anon means soon. See them on the right? Here is a tip: read the line aloud, find the verb, and swap the old words for new ones. Thou hast a kind heart. What does that mean?
Well done! Shakespeare is also the earliest known writer of words we still use. Look at the board: bedroom, lonely, eyeball. Challenge: next time you feel lonely, remember Shakespeare wrote it first!

faq.a: Wherefore means why, not where. When Juliet says wherefore art thou Romeo, she is asking why he has to be a Montague.

faq.q: Why is Shakespeare hard to read?
faq.a: He wrote around 1600 in Early Modern English. Some words have changed meaning, and he often puts words in an unusual order to fit the rhythm of his lines.
Thou means you when you are talking to one person, often a friend, family member or someone younger. Thee is the object form, and thy means your.
His plays have the earliest known uses of many words, such as bedroom, lonely, eyeball and swagger. Some may have been spoken before, but he is the first to have written them down.

faq.q: How do I understand a Shakespeare line?
faq.a: Read it aloud, find the verb and who is doing it, swap old words for modern ones, and use the notes in your edition. Watching a performance helps a lot.

facts: Shakespeare lived from 1564 to 1616 and wrote about 37 plays and 154 sonnets.
Shakespeare's English is Early Modern English, not Old English, which is much older and looks like a foreign language.

quiz.say: In Wherefore art thou Romeo?, what does wherefore mean?
quiz.show: In Wherefore art thou Romeo?, what does wherefore mean?
quiz.why: Juliet asks why he is Romeo, a Montague.

wrong.0: This is the common mistake; wherefore asks the reason.
wrong.1: Wherefore is about the reason, not the time.

quiz.say: What is the modern way to say Thou art kind?
quiz.show: What is the modern way to say Thou art kind?
quiz.why: Thou means you, and art means are.

wrong.2: Thou is the person spoken to, not the speaker.
